objective: Plan five additional articles, bringing Spek's published total from two to seven, with at most one approved publication per day.

status: Research and proposed calendar only; no new article, automation, scheduled publication, or paid campaign created.

published.title: How to translate a menu on your iPhone
Egyptian Arabic translator apps for iPhone: what to choose

proposedCadence.rule: Approval and verification before publication. If not ready, move the date; never catch up by publishing two on one day. Dates are proposed targets, not scheduled jobs.
proposedCadence.googleClarification: One-per-day is an editorial preference, not a published Google safety threshold. Quality, originality, accuracy and purpose matter.

method.keywordPlanner: 40 manually supplied English keyword phrases; Google Search; All languages (UI locked); All locations and United States separately; October 2025–September 2026.
method.gum: Used existing jobhunter profile for Search Console reads. Ads scope remains unavailable; keyword ranges came from the existing Chrome account. No credentials, scopes or billing changed.
method.trends: Compared the five selected primary search terms worldwide over the past 12 months; stored all 53 displayed weekly rows and excluded the newest incomplete week from window means.
method.resultReview: Reviewed current search-result types and official Apple, Google, WhatsApp, DeepL, SpanishDictionary and NICT sources. App-vendor comparisons are treated as competition signals, not independent accuracy evidence.
limitations: Rounded ranges including close variants; do not sum keywords or convert volumes into traffic forecasts.
Google Ads competition is advertiser competition, not an organic SEO score.
Search snapshots are not a geo-controlled Google top-ten or backlink audit.
No third-party-app hands-on benchmark or native-speaker evaluation was performed.
No ChatGPT/Claude prompt-demand measurement or recommendation guarantee.
A dash in Keyword Planner means no available metric, not zero demand.
Trends is sampled relative interest, not volume. Low-data zeros and isolated spikes do not establish no demand or recurring seasonality.

trends.scope: Worldwide; Past 12 months; All categories; Web Search; search terms
limitations: Relative sampled 0–100 indices, not search counts or percentages.
Newest week excluded from descriptive window means.
One-year sample does not establish recurring seasonality or causation.

siteData.interpretation: Too small and too early for topic-level prioritization; the recent publication is not yet a performance experiment with enough observations.

topics.title: How to translate a screenshot on your iPhone
topics.intent: Complete a saved-screen translation task; troubleshoot missing text recognition.
topics.reason: Broadens coverage beyond Arabic and makes direct use of Spek Photo Library import, while teaching the built-in path first.
topics.distinctContribution: Show saved app screens and screenshots, a legibility check, and what to try when Live Text does not appear. Link to the menu article instead of repeating a restaurant-camera tutorial.
outline: Quick choice by screenshot type and supported language
Photos and Apple Translate steps
Gallery alternatives when the built-in path is unavailable
Missing Translate / Live Text troubleshooting, crop and legibility
What each method needs online and on-device
evidenceBeforePublication: Verify each photographed control on the current version or label it documentation-based.
Use owned non-private sample screenshots; record language, device/iOS, app version and chosen method.
Separate OCR support from translation-language support; do not promise all on-screen text will translate.
topics.spekRole: One clearly disclosed Photo Library option; no claim to overlay or automatically translate another running app.
topics.competitionAssessment: Apple support, videos and troubleshooting discussions already address this. The useful angle is an exact screenshot workflow with current limits, not a generic image article.
topics.priority: First because it is an actionable cross-language guide and can be prepared without inventing dialect examples.
topics.confidence: Good product fit; modest exact iPhone phrase demand and weak Trends signal.

topics.title: Mexican Spanish translator apps for iPhone: choosing the right Spanish
topics.intent: Choose a translation workflow and understand country-specific versus general Spanish output.
topics.reason: Strongest measured broad translation demand among the selected language topics, including substantial US demand; supports the product's broad coverage.
topics.distinctContribution: Distinguish a Mexico output choice, Latin American dictionary labels and a playback-accent setting. Those are different capabilities.
outline: Quick choice for conversation, message wording or vocabulary lookup
Mexico versus a general Spanish label, without claiming other varieties are unusable
Feature comparison: country choice, voice, text, dictionary context and connectivity
How to select Mexico in Spek; ownership disclosure
When to check phrasing with a fluent Mexican Spanish speaker
evidenceBeforePublication: Verify Mexico selection in Spek and document which other apps expose regional output versus pronunciation settings.
Use matched test inputs only if showing outputs or declaring a winner; get fluent Mexican Spanish review for published examples.
Do not use the 10K–100K English-to-Mexican head term as the projected audience of an app-comparison article.
topics.spekRole: Explicit Mexico / Spanish (Mexican) country choice, with its actual hold-to-speak workflow.
topics.competitionAssessment: Broad terms often expect an instant translator or dictionary, not a blog article. Explicit app-shopping phrases are much smaller; no easy organic win is assumed.
topics.priority: Second to demonstrate non-Arabic regional coverage with real demand.
topics.confidence: Strong broad demand and product fit; lower confidence about how much of that demand wants an app comparison.

topics.title: European Portuguese translator apps for iPhone: choosing Portuguese for Portugal
topics.intent: Choose translation for Portugal and understand the distinction between output variety and spoken playback.
topics.reason: Smaller but specific task, aligned with Spek's Portugal and Brazil choices. The current Apple Translate availability labels provide a concrete issue to explain.
topics.distinctContribution: Make the European/Brazilian output and pronunciation distinction explicit; include DeepL as a credible alternative, not only Apple/Google/Spek.
outline: What to choose for Portugal: text, voice or photo task
Where Portuguese variety is explicitly selectable
Comparison of output label, playback, dictation, photo handling and purchases
Selecting Portugal in Spek
When a native speaker or human translator is needed
evidenceBeforePublication: Check current DeepL iPhone language picker and Portuguese variety choices for text, dictation and playback separately.
Confirm the current Apple availability list at writing time; absence of a separate Portugal label is not an accuracy test.
Have a fluent European Portuguese reviewer validate any examples; otherwise keep the comparison documentation-based.

topics.competitionAssessment: Existing commercial Portuguese comparisons and learning-app results overlap. Make this about translation choices for Portugal, not another general language-learning list.

topics.title: How to translate an in-person conversation on iPhone
topics.intent: Two people taking turns on one phone, rather than phone-call, FaceTime or AirPods translation.
topics.reason: Covers voice separately from photo translation and creates a practical parent guide for language-specific choices.
topics.distinctContribution: Separate Apple's Conversation mode, Google live or conversation features, and Spek's manual hold-and-release turns. Show exact requirements rather than calling every option real time.
outline: Quick setup for two people sharing one phone
Apple Conversation and face-to-face options
Google's current iPhone conversation and live feature availability
Spek hold, release, review and swap workflow
Noise, names, short turns and offline preparation
Separate note on calls, FaceTime and AirPods requirements
evidenceBeforePublication: Check current iPhone UI and region requirements, especially Google features announced in September 2026.
Document turn-taking and audio playback with a non-private sample exchange.
Do not imply Spek translates phone calls, runs continuous background interpretation, or works offline.
topics.spekRole: A deliberate turn-by-turn voice option with country choices, with internet and in-app purchase requirements clear.
topics.competitionAssessment: Apple support and many app vendors already serve this intent. The broader live-translation phrase mixes hardware and calling needs and is excluded from the primary demand estimate.
topics.priority: Fourth, after two additional regional guides are available to link to.
topics.confidence: Strong product fit; modest exact iPhone keyword volume. Relative Trends interest was higher late in the window, without a causal or traffic forecast.

Keep recognition, translation output, playback accent, dictionary region labels and offline support separate.

Do not bump editorial updated dates for cosmetic links alone.
